scenario.fault_family: link cut (both fabric uplinks of one leaf)
scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) reports a total outage: nothing across the
fabric responds, and pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) cannot reach pc_0_1 either.
pc_0_1 CAN still ping its own gateway 10.0.1.1, and leaf_router_0_1
itself is up and reachable on its console -- its FRR daemons are all
running. Both of its BGP sessions to the spines are gone. Diagnose.

injection.command:
ip link set eth0 down
  ip link set eth1 down

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP
ip -br link show eth1 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_1 eth0 and eth1 -- BOTH fabric
  uplinks: eth0 (172.16.0.7/31, link subnet 172.16.0.6/31) to
  spine_router_0_0 and eth1 (172.16.0.11/31, link subnet
  172.16.0.10/31) to spine_router_0_1
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_1's only paths into the CLOS fabric are its
  two spine uplinks. With both interfaces down, both BGP sessions drop
  and the leaf can neither learn 10.0.0.0/24 nor deliver its own
  10.0.1.0/24 traffic anywhere -- the CLOS redundancy is defeated
  because BOTH members of the redundant pair are down. The host-facing
  port eth2 (10.0.1.1/24) is untouched, so pc_0_1 still reaches its
  gateway but nothing beyond it. Note this is the one link-fault shape
  where redundancy does not save the leaf; a single downed uplink
  would only degrade redundancy.
Localization: leaf_router_0_1
Root cause: both spine-facing interfaces (eth0, eth1) down on
  leaf_router_0_1
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` and `ip link set eth1 up` on
  leaf_router_0_1; both BGP sessions re-establish on their own.
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth0 up && ip link set eth1 up` on leaf_router_0_1. Once
the uplinks are UP the sessions to both spines come back and pc_0_1
regains fabric reachability.
scoring_axes: must-identify-affected-links: BOTH spine uplinks down -- eth0 (to spine_router_0_0) AND eth1 (to spine_router_0_1)

bonus-notes-host-link-fine: explicitly rules out the host access link / pc_0_1 itself (eth2 UP, gateway pingable)

agent.diagnosis_text:
Both uplink interfaces of leaf_router_0_1 — eth0 (toward spine_router_0_0:eth2,
172.16.0.6/31) and eth1 (toward spine_router_0_1:eth2, 172.16.0.11/31) — were
administratively shut down at the Linux kernel level. The kernel interface flags
show <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> without the UP bit on both ports, meaning they are
admin-down, not merely link-down. FRR's own interface view confirms "Interface
eth0 is down" and "Interface eth1 is down", both with "Link ups: 0 (never)" and
a single link-down event timestamped 2026/08/03 05:49:48 — the moment the BGP
sessions collapsed. The protodown field is off on both, ruling out any FRR
protocol-triggered shutdown; this was a raw OS-level action (ip link set eth0
down / ip link set eth1 down). Both spine-facing ports on spine_router_0_0 and
spine_router_0_1 are fully UP/LOWER_UP, so the fault is entirely local to
leaf_router_0_1. With both uplinks dead, FRR's BGP process has no reachable
next-hops for the peer addresses, keeping both sessions permanently in Active
state. leaf_router_0_1's RIB retains only its directly connected 10.0.1.0/24,
so it cannot forward traffic toward any other subnet — explaining why pc_0_1 can
reach its gateway (eth2 is still UP) but is completely isolated from the rest of
the fabric.

Root cause: Both kernel-level uplink interfaces (eth0, eth1) on leaf_router_0_1
were shut down, dropping both eBGP sessions and all fabric routes.

Corrective fix: On leaf_router_0_1, run `ip link set eth0 up && ip link set eth1
up`. BGP will re-establish to both spines within seconds (hold-timer is already
counting), the full prefix table will be re-learned, and end-to-end connectivity
between pc_0_0 and pc_0_1 will be restored. To make it persistent across
restarts, ensure the startup configuration (e.g. /etc/network/interfaces or
equivalent) does not issue a link-down on those interfaces.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies leaf_router_0_1 as the affected device in multiple places.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-affected-links: BOTH spine uplinks down -- eth0 (to spine_router_0_0) AND eth1 (to spine_router_0_1)
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names both uplinks—eth0 to spine_router_0_0 and eth1 to spine_router_0_1—on leaf_router_0_1 as administratively down.

per_axis.axis: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: pc_0_1 still reaches its gateway (host link fine) but nothing past the leaf
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly notes eth2/10.0.1.0/24 remains up and that pc_0_1 can reach its gateway while no routes beyond the leaf exist, matching the symptom pattern.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-host-link-fine: explicitly rules out the host access link / pc_0_1 itself (eth2 UP, gateway pingable)
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states eth2 is still UP and pc_0_1 can reach its gateway, ruling out the host access link as the problem.
The agent explicitly instructs to bring eth0 and eth1 up on leaf_router_0_1 (ip link set ... up) and to persist the change, which matches the expected fix.

Investigation log shows both leaf uplinks administratively down while spine ports remain up, FRR interfaces report no link ups and RIB only contains the host subnet — the writeup's conclusions follow directly from those observations with minimal unsupported claims.
